notes:
- **Every frame of a bunch on a screen that reports late.** After a hold-up on the network the Mac viewer sent the next frame to its screen only once the screen had said it showed the one before. On a MacBook's 120 Hz display that word can come just before the next refresh (in the last benchmark, 7 ms after the frame), so the frames of a bunch went out at half the screen's rate, 60 a second, and the rest were left out. Where the word comes that late the viewer now sends the next frame at the refresh without waiting for it. Where it comes promptly nothing changes.
- **A change you cause is on the screen sooner:** for 2 seconds after a key, a click or a scroll the viewer asks the screen for its full rate. In a still picture the display had taken 19 to 29 ms to show a new frame, against 5 ms in motion.
- **The host's log says how many frames went ahead of the screen's word.**

The third needs RexDesk Host 0.9.2 on the Mac you connect to.
